name: Yrsa Stormborn
equipment: A Valmont Legion campaign token (a stamped lead disc, the mercenary contract version — not official, not quite desertion)
A small ivory tusk-bead on a cord at her wrist (carved with a name in Orcish script)
features: Darkvision (Half-Orc racial — you can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light; you can't discern color in darkness, only shades of grey)
Menacing (Half-Orc racial — you gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill; already counted in skills list)

Relentless Endurance (Half-Orc racial — when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead; once per long rest; this keeps you standing when other characters would be unconscious and making death saving throws)

Savage Attacks (Half-Orc racial — when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit; effectively adds one extra damage die on a crit)

Rage (Barbarian level 1 — in battle, you fight with primal ferocity; on your turn you can enter a rage as a bonus action; while raging you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, a +2 bonus to melee damage rolls using Strength, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; your rage lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you are knocked unconscious, or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then; you can rage 2 times per long rest at level 1)

Unarmored Defense (Barbarian level 1 — while not wearing armor, your armor class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier; you can use a shield and still gain this benefit; Yrsa's AC unarmored: 10 + 1 + 3 = 14, and she has no shield equipped)

Military Rank (Soldier background — you hold the rank of veteran soldier in Valmont's mercenary auxiliaries; you can invoke your soldier's authority in dealings with other military personnel of that faction, though your current status as a contract-expired mercenary operating independently complicates this)

personality.traits: I say what I mean and mean what I say, and I find the Coronne habit of saying the opposite of what one means so exhausting that I have developed a headache I cannot shake. I laugh too loudly and drink whatever is put in front of me. I respect anyone who can hit, run, or endure without complaining, and I do not much respect anything else as a primary qualification.
personality.ideals: I have fought for coin and I have fought for principle and the coin is cleaner because it doesn't pretend to be something it isn't. But if coin is all a thing is, it's a small thing. The people who fight for nothing but coin tend to be the ones who do the worst of what armies do. I would rather have a reason, even a complicated one.
personality.bonds: The tusk-bead on my wrist was carved by my mother and given to me when I left the marches. She died three years ago, a month before I could get back to see her. I carry the bead because she carried one when she was a fighter and because I have nothing else of her. I will not discuss this with anyone.
personality.flaws: I am deeply, constitutionally suspicious of anyone who uses more words than necessary, which in Coronne means almost everyone, which means I spend most of my time suspecting people before I have evidence and being only sometimes wrong. I also drink when I am bored and I am frequently bored in cities.

appearance: Yrsa Stormborn is six feet and change of half-Orc soldiery, broad and solid in the manner of someone built for endurance rather than elegance, with the dense, close-packed muscle of a fighter who has worked hard since childhood. Her skin is a warm grey-green, darker at the jaw and neck where her Orc heritage concentrates, and her lower canines jut a half-inch past her upper lip — not dramatically, as on a full Orc, but enough to give her resting expression a permanent quality of mild threat that she uses professionally. Her hair is dark, coarse, and kept in a single heavy braid that falls to the middle of her back and is wrapped at intervals with leather cord; she unbraids it before combat, which has the practical effect of making her look significantly larger and the theatrical effect of terrifying whoever is watching. Her eyes are a bright amber-yellow, warm and alert, at odds with the rest of her face, which is scarred at the jaw from an axe blow in the Valmont campaigns and at the left brow from a bar fight in the Pont Sange garrison town. She does not wear armor as a matter of preference and philosophy, which is fine because she does not need it — she moves differently without it, faster and lower, with a rolling, coiled quality that combat veterans read correctly as someone who knows what they are doing. The greataxe rides on her back in a harness of her own construction, and the two handaxes are at her belt. The ivory tusk-bead is on her left wrist and is the only ornament she wears.
backstory:
The Stormborn name is a translation, roughly, of the Orcish clan-word for those born during the storms that roll off the Valmont marches in early spring — cold, violent storms that come fast and leave nothing undecided. Yrsa was born during one such storm, her mother said, which is why the lightning does not frighten her and other loud things do not much either.

The marches of Valmont are contested country: fertile enough to be worth having, remote enough to be poorly defended, close enough to the Dragonborn principalities and the free city-states to the north that the question of who they belong to has been answered differently in different generations. Half-Orcs are not uncommon there — generations of Orc raiders, Orc settlers, and human border communities have produced a population that is thoroughly mixed and at no one's ease about it. Yrsa's mother was a caravan guard; her father was a soldier in one of Valmont's frontier garrisons; they separated before she was old enough to know him as a presence rather than an absence. Her mother raised her in a settlement that changed hands three times before Yrsa was twenty and taught her the relevant skill for that environment: be useful to whoever has the power, and be good enough that the next set of people with power will want to keep you.

She enlisted in the Valmont mercenary auxiliaries at seventeen. The auxiliaries are not the Duke's legions — they are the expedient second option, the bodies that take the contested ground before the legions come in to hold it. They pay in coin and loot rights and ask no questions about the soldiers they recruit. Yrsa was an auxiliary for six years and rose to something approaching a senior rank by being harder to kill than almost anyone and better at keeping people alive than most.

She came to Coronne on the tail of a contract that brought a company of auxiliaries to the capital's garrison district during the early days of the succession crisis — Valmont was positioning forces, and that meant money for soldiers willing to spend time in the city. Yrsa spent three months of it finding the city exactly as alienating as she had expected: too many people saying too little directly, too much money in too few hands, too much contempt running downward and too much performance running upward. She liked the Shamble, in the way you like a place that is at least honest about what it is.

Her contract expired two weeks ago. She has not re-enlisted, which means she is in a city she does not much like with no employment and a choice to make about which direction to walk. The fire in the Old Quarter was not a choice — she was in the street when the buildings went up and ran toward it because running toward fire is what she does — but what came out of the burning alley afterward was a choice of a kind she has not made before. Not a contract. Not a soldier's order. Something that felt, uncomfortably, like a reason.
